title: Choose the visual world for the operator desk
question: The roll assigned the catalogue-card world for the inbox-first build. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Catalogue Card & Stamp Trail
options.lineage: library card catalogues and due-date stamps
options.thesis: Every conversation is a catalogue card, and everything the system did to it is stamped onto the record.
options.viewport: Buckram-green rail on the left; drawer tabs across the queue; card rows carrying a stamp trail; the record card and stamp sheet beside the thread.
options.risk: Archive warmth reads as nostalgia if the tables are not strictly modern in behaviour.

raised.raise: Coded strip, decoded on demand: the stamp trail is compressed to tick marks in the ruled margin until hover or focus spells the full sentence.
Mono-ink data field: the day's traffic is drawn as one rail of lines, and colour appears only where it carries meaning.
A fixed state language sits beneath the work: conversation states are a stable frame that the queue's active item is plotted into, never edits.
Fixed-scale comparison: every card row keeps identical field positions and row height, so the eye compares instead of re-reading.
Connected stage trail: the record draws the path an item took as a connected sequence, not a sentence.

options.label: Triage Strip
options.lineage: hospital triage boards and acuity tags
options.thesis: The queue is sorted by who needs a person, and the colour of the tag is the promise.
options.viewport: Dark top bar, acuity legend, one strip of ranked rows with a colour tag on every row, vitals panel on the right.
options.risk: Also where most runs in this category land: everyone understands a triage board, so it is effective and familiar rather than distinctive.

options.label: Grid Specimen Index
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel grid specimens and modular index sheets
options.thesis: The desk is a published grid: every record occupies a named cell, and the specimen's counts are the operator's dashboard.
options.viewport: Faint blueprint grid under a heavy squarish display word; the queue as a ruled index whose rows carry a count and a plus; system counts strip along the bottom rail.
options.risk: A specimen is an argument about structure, not a place to work; unrelieved stencil display type turns every heading into a poster.
options.case: Fuses sharply: a specimen is literally a table of records with counts, which is the desk's real content, and cell discipline kills the row-drift this table lives with. Loses narrowly on warmth, since the operator hand-writes human summaries into these rows all day.
options.kept: Every element sits in a named cell of a published grid; nothing floats.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: The day's traffic is one calibrated rail of lines; a line's position is when it landed and its colour is its state, and state is the only colour allowed.
options.viewport: Two-line instrument nav down the left; a full-width rail of vertical lines with a wavelength-style time axis beneath it; instrument panels of large numerals over a real-time feed sparkline.
options.risk: Instrument darkness is a specialist's room; an operator reading human sentences all day pays for the black in fatigue, and the rail cannot render a long message.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: traffic, timing and state are exactly the desk's three numbers, and a rail is the only honest picture of a queue's shape over a day. Loses on identification, because instrument panels make the product read as monitoring software rather than a place where people talk.
options.kept: One rail as the only time axis; colour reserved for state, never for decoration.

options.label: Star Atlas & Fix
options.lineage: star atlases and plotted observation charts
options.thesis: The desk is a chart: the coordinate frame is fixed and published, and each conversation is an object plotted into it with a magnitude that says how loudly it needs a person.
options.viewport: Atlas-dark ground; a coordinate frame with hour and degree ticks ruling the queue; each record a plotted dot keyed by magnitude; the opened record annotated beside the thread in italic serif with notation rows.
options.risk: Chart notation is a language the operator must be taught, and a magnitude scale risks making a waiting customer feel like an astronomy exercise.
options.case: Fuses sharply: a fixed frame that records are plotted into without editing it is precisely how a queue and its state vocabulary should relate. Loses narrowly on legibility, since hairline chart rules at queue density thin out on the laptop screens this desk actually uses.
options.kept: A fixed coordinate frame that records are plotted into, never edited by them.

options.label: Dark Ops Console
options.thesis: The pipeline is the product: items move through connected stages, and every stage reports its own status inline.
options.viewport: Icon rail, dark panels in a three-column grid, a row of connected stage nodes, a right column of recent activity.
options.risk: This is where most runs in this category land, and the darkness makes an ops desk feel like a developer tool while the day's real subject is a person waiting on a reply.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the console's subject is a deployment, and its monospace density optimises for scanning logs, not for writing a careful sentence to a customer.
options.kept: Connected stage rails: the path an item took is drawn as a sequence, not described in a sentence.

options.label: Stage Folio
options.lineage: botanical folios following one plant through its seasons
options.thesis: A conversation is a folio of numbered stages, each with a written caption, so its position in the process is never guessed.
options.viewport: Parchment ground, a left index of stages, the queue's active record shown as five numbered plates with season captions beneath.
options.risk: Sequence is not how a queue is read: items are handled out of order, and a quiet plate ground fights live counters that must move every minute.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the world's subject is ordered growth, while a refund waiting since yesterday is the desk's subject, and the folio has no vocabulary for urgency.
options.kept: Numbered stages with a written caption under each, so process position is legible at a glance.

options.label: Guide Map & Gates
options.lineage: visitor guide maps with named gates and routes
options.thesis: The account is territory: conversations are stops on a route, and every stop is named with its outcome.
options.viewport: Cream ground with soft colour fields, gate pills marking queue sections, rounded tile list of stops, one tall route panel on the right.
options.risk: The ground is consumer wayfinding, and organic fields make the strict row comparison this table depends on harder to read than a ruled grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hospitality is the world's promise and a refund queue is the product's reality; pastel gates cannot mark a handoff that is overdue.
options.kept: A labelled route with gates: territory, stops and outcomes named in one picture.

canonCard.label: The category standard, executed impeccably
canonCard.thesis: A neutral product UI: white ground, one blue accent, a clean sidebar and a table.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, header, cards of key numbers, a tidy conversation list.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
